subject: Procurement & packaging next steps — Redwood / Acme
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Chen <samantha@acme-products.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Procurement & packaging next steps — Redwood / Acme

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so procurement has what they need: 

Summary of needs:
- Primary use: customer-facing personalization & search features (low-latency text generation + embeddings).
- Estimated steady-state usage: ~5M tokens/month with peaks during campaigns.
- Data handling: no PHI, but must be within Acme VPC for production-grade PII controls (eventual Private deployment considered).

Procurement questions we flagged on the call:
1) Preferred payment method: PO (net 30) vs card?
2) Will you require marketplace procurement (AWS Marketplace) or direct vendor invoicing?
3) Any required contract/legal clauses or insurance limits we should know about?

Packaging options to consider (high level):
- Hosted (on-demand): fastest to start, card or invoice billing, usage pricing per token. Good for POC/pilot.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): committed monthly/annual GPU capacity, lower unit cost for steady throughput, supports PO/contracting.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): for regulated workloads, requires longer lead time and license/enterprise agreement.

Attachments: I attached a short pricing & packaging overview (redwood_pricing_options.pdf) that maps typical usage profiles to hosted/dedicated/private recommendations.

Proposed next steps:
- Can procurement confirm PO vs card and marketplace preference? (procurement@acme-products.com is fine to loop in)
- If PO: we'll send a formal quote and SOW for review. If card: we can enable a trial immediately.
- I'll loop in Aditya (solutions) for sizing and any security questionnaire items.

Would love confirmation on preferred billing path so we can align commercial and procurement docs.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: redwood_pricing_options.pdf (1 page summary)

From: Samantha Chen <samantha@acme-products.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-products.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Procurement & packaging next steps — Redwood / Acme

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap — this is helpful. A couple quick answers from procurement: 
- Preferred payment path: PO (net 30) for anything beyond pilot.
- Marketplace: We generally prefer to buy via AWS Marketplace for easier internal approvals, but procurement can make exceptions for strategic vendors if PO terms are standard.
- Contract: our standard procurement team will send over the questionnaire and require standard indemnity and data processing language; I attached the procurement questionnaire for completeness.

A few clarifying questions from me: 
1) For the dedicated vs hosted recommendation — what minimum commit would you expect for predictable latency at our estimated volume?
2) If we go through Marketplace, does Redwood support Marketplace metered billing or private offers (contract + Marketplace)?
3) Is there a shorter path to start a pilot (card-based trial) while procurement completes the PO?

CCing procurement@acme-products.com so they see the thread.

Best,
Samantha Chen
Head of Product — Personalization
Acme Products

Attachment: acme_procurement_questionnaire.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Chen <samantha@acme-products.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Procurement & packaging next steps — Redwood / Acme

Thanks Samantha — super helpful. Looping in Aditya (solutions engineer) to provide sizing guidance and Logan (sales ops) to confirm billing path and Marketplace support. See answers below and next steps: 

Aditya — can you weigh in on the commit sizing? For ~5M tokens/month with moderate peaks, would recommend Dedicated with a 3–6 month initial commit to hit consistent latency SLAs. For initial pilot we can run Hosted on-demand and enable prefix caching to reduce cost; Aditya can propose a Dedicated config (gpus/instances + expected throughput).

Logan — Acme prefers PO and Marketplace is possible. Do we support AWS Marketplace private offers (contract + PO) for enterprise accounts? If so, what's the expected turnaround and any fee differences vs direct invoicing?

Samantha — regarding pilot path: yes, we can start a short card-based pilot (30 days, limited capacity) while procurement completes PO. If procurement prefers Marketplace, we can draft a private offer but that will add a week or two for setup.

Action items:
- Aditya: provide 1-page Dedicated sizing + recommended commit range and estimated unit cost (due EOD Tue).
- Logan: confirm Marketplace support and billing lead time (due EOD Tue).
- Marissa: prepare formal quote + SOW for PO path once we have commit range.

Thanks — we'll aim to have the sizing + commercial path for your procurement team by tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: procurement@acme-products.com
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Chen <samantha@acme-products.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Procurement & packaging next steps — Redwood / Acme

Hi Marissa / Aditya / Logan —

Thanks for looping us in. Quick confirmation from procurement: PO (net 30) is our operating model for production purchases. Marketplace via AWS is preferred if Redwood can accept a private offer with a contract incorporated — that streamlines approvals. A few items we need to see on the formal quote/SOW: 
- PO instructions (billing address & remit)
- Line-itemized pricing (monthly commit vs on-demand rates)
- Term and renewal model (monthly vs annual commits)
- Data handling & security attestation (SOC 2, logging/audit options)

We attached our questionnaire. Please include the above in the quote or indicate where they will be covered in the contract.

Next steps for us: once we receive a tailored quote + SOW and confirmation of Marketplace private offer capability, we can issue a PO within ~7–10 business days. If you can provide a short card-based pilot agreement to start earlier, procurement will accept that for the trial only.

Regards,
Acme Procurement Team
procurement@acme-products.com
